query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In the as-built laser-powder bed–fused Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy, cellular micro-segregation leaves a continuous three-dimensional network of Cr–Ti-rich interdendritic films. During exposure to hot oxidising or reducing gases (800–1000 °C, PO2 ≥10-6 atm or PH2 ≥10-1 atm) these films become preferential, fast-diffusion paths for oxygen (or hydrogen) and transform first into (Cr,Ti)-rich σ/χ intermetallics and then into porous mixed oxides (or brittle hydrides). Once ≥70 % of the film network converts, a continuous brittle layer surrounds each fcc cell, producing strain localisation and rapid interlinkage of cracks that triggers catastrophic, low-ductility failure. Eliminating the segregated films before exposure will therefore suppress both the accelerated mass-loss rate and the sudden fracture.
generation.material_initial_state: As-built LPBF Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy with ∼0.5–1 µm cellular substructure, Cr–Ti enrichment (≈+20–30 % over matrix) at cell walls, residual porosity <1 vol %, single-phase fcc matrix with fine L1₂ (γ′) precipitates
generation.intervention: Apply a 20 min homogenisation heat treatment at 1200 °C followed by water quench to dissolve interdendritic segregation and break up the Cr–Ti-rich film network (confirmed by STEM-EDS showing <5 % composition gradients).
generation.conditions: Isothermal exposure for 100 h in either (a) dry air (PO2≈0.21 atm) or (b) 1 atm H2, at 900 °C, followed by tensile testing at 25 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Continuity and chemistry of the Cr–Ti-rich interdendritic network inherited from solidification.
generation.mechanism: 1. Segregated Cr/Ti lowers local chemical potentials, making films the preferred sink for diffusing O or H. 2. Rapid inward diffusion along these films nucleates σ/χ phase; subsequent internal oxidation/hydriding embrittles the network. 3. Once the brittle products percolate, plastic incompatibility between softened fcc cells and rigid films localises strains, producing inter-cell cracking and abrupt failure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared with the baseline as-built alloy, the homogenised condition will show: • at least 2× lower mass-gain (air) or mass-loss (H2) per unit area after 100 h; • no continuous σ/oxide/hydride films on cross-section; • room-temperature tensile elongation ≥10 % (vs ≤1 % and sudden fracture for the baseline).
generation.baseline: As-built specimens exposed under the same atmospheres exhibit 3–5 mg cm-2 mass change, continuous Cr-Ti oxide/hydride films and brittle failure at <1 % strain.
generation.boundary: Temperature window 800–1000 °C where σ/χ precipitation kinetics are fast; below 750 °C the transformation is too slow and both conditions retain ductility, above 1050 °C films dissolve regardless of pre-treatment, so differences vanish.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of the mass-change reduction (2×) is estimated; the critical 70 % film conversion threshold has not been directly measured and may vary.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of LPBF coupons (as-built vs homogenised). Expose both sets for 100 h at 900 °C in flowing dry air or H2. Measure (i) mass change every 20 h, (ii) cross-sectional microstructure by SEM/EDS and EBSD, (iii) room-temperature tensile curves.
measurements: Area fraction of σ/χ or oxide/hydride along cell walls (%)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If homogenised samples still develop a continuous (>80 %) Cr-Ti-rich σ/oxide/hydride network AND show mass change and tensile elongation within ±10 % of the as-built baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
